quest.title: Stained Spots
quest.description: If the hem of a skirt is stained, can it still take the stage?
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x600, Mora x39350, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x9

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chiori! We're here!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Oh, you're here early. I haven't even opened the shop yet.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, has Kirara left already?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Yep. With the Special Patrol, bright and early.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did everything go alright on the road?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: I believe so. The Patrol makes for quite the entourage.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: The way they marched forward with Kirara in the center, you'd think she was some sort of VIP. For the second leg, the Spina also came with a pretty large group, led by Navia herself.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: They took care to clear the path beforehand as well. Kirara won't so much as step on a single stray rock on her journey.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: I even heard that Navia decided out of the blue to make a batch of macarons as a going-away gift for Kirara. An excellent souvenir to remember Fontaine by, I'd say.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like Navia really got into it!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: My thoughts exactly. She even lamented the fact that she didn't have time to prepare something even fancier. I'm pretty sure she can't wait for another escort opportunity to come her way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y'know, now that you mention Navia, Paimon thinks the two of you are actually pretty similar... You say what you mean, and when you have an idea, you really hit the ground running...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: I suppose that's why we're such good friends.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Navia has a certain resilience about her — it's part of who she is. No matter what comes her way, she never bows down in the face of adversity. That sort of determination and courage is something I really admire.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: That same spirit is the true vision of my brand. When she first mentioned commissioning an outfit from my boutique... Well, I'm sure you can imagine my excitement.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's like finding the perfect brand ambassador, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Indeed. Customers pay attention not just to the clothes, but also to the figures in society who wear said clothes. People like to copy the styles of those they look up to.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, and here Paimon thought all that mattered was for the clothes to look cute...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Fashion is about more than just looks, my dear — especially if you've got your sights set on a market the size of Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: ...Hmm? Well, would you look at the time...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh yeah! Come on, let's get down to business. We're here to model!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Indeed. Give me a moment while I go retrieve some fabrics and sample outfits. Why don't you help me set up the shop displays in the meantime?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Set them up... Uh, how exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Just carefully organize the ready-to-wear clothes with an eye toward their types and styles. This way, we can guarantee that the customers will see something different every day.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... There sure is a lot that goes into running a store!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Well then, I'll leave the displays to you.

dialogues.speaker: Eloffe
dialogues.text: Miss Chiori isn't the sort to just give up. She probably just needs a place where she can think in peace.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Good job. That should do it.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Chiori! Are you alright? Sorry for taking so long, I got caught up and... Whoa! Wh—What happened to your shop?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Who did this!? Those monsters... Slandering you in the papers wasn't enough for them, was it? They even sent people to wreck your shop...!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Give me their names! Since they're all too eager to tear up other people's clothes, I think it's about time the Spina di Rosula returned the favor!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: M—Maybe you should calm down a bit first, cause you see, um...

choices.text: I—I was the one who did it...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Huh...? HUH?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: #What is this, a soap opera? I was the one who asked {NICKNAME} to tear up the outfits. We need all the fabrics and accessories we can get.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Oh, so that's... what happened... Ahaha... Guess I got a bit ahead of myself just now. Back to what you were doing, everyone. You can all just pretend like I didn't say anything...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Navia sure is scary when she's angry...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: If there's one thing I can't stand, it's a false accusation. No one's gonna orchestrate some conspiracy to take down one of my friends and get away with it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You and Chiori are really close!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Of course! Everyone knows that Chiori makes the most gorgeous outfits in town. All of the Spina di Rosula's formal wear is custom-tailored here!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Now, if only you'd give me the contract for your uniforms as well...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Pfft, as if you'd enjoy designing something as boring and formulaic as a uniform. That's why I didn't ask you in the first place, silly.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Plus, with how much your intel has helped us out in the past, to the Spina, you're more of an intelligence agency than a fashion boutique.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: If I had it my way, it would be the other way around...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Anyway, we both know why I'm here. Tell me, how can the Spina be of service to you?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: ...If it's not too much trouble, can I borrow some skilled hands to help with some simple sewing work? I'll need all the help I can get if I'm going to finish these outfits over the next few days.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: No problem. I've got a few of those guys all ready to go! I just knew you wouldn't be intimidated into withdrawing from this year's show.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: When are you going to get started? I can help with the sewing, too.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Actually, there's something else I'd like to ask of you.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Ask away. I'm all ears!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: #Oh and, {NICKNAME} and Paimon — could you help me pass word to Lyney and Lynette? I'll need their help as well.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Gladly.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: I'm done with my interview! Has Miss Chiori made it back yet— Aahhhh!! What happened to the boutique!?

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Who did this!? Give me names! I'll make sure every last one lands a full feature on the front page of the Steambird tomorrow!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Not this again...

choices.text: Boss... Please, go easy on us...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Anyway, let's move on to the real task at hand.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Over here, stand still. I'll take your measurements first...

dialogues.speaker: Leeann
dialogues.text: ...Excuse me, Miss Chiori.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Oh, good morning, Leeann. How have you been recently?

dialogues.speaker: Leeann
dialogues.text: Umm... Not too bad.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Your gown will be ready next week, so there's no need to worry about missing the ball. Or did you come here today because you'd like to make a new request, perhaps?

dialogues.speaker: Leeann
dialogues.text: Oh... No... Nothing like that, Miss Chiori. To be honest... I came here today to cancel my order for that gown.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: ...Cancel your order?

dialogues.speaker: Leeann
dialogues.text: Uh, but you can keep the deposit, of course! I know you can't return any materials you've already used.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Don't worry about the materials. I'm more concerned about you. Did something happen, Leeann? Have your plans changed?

dialogues.speaker: Leeann
dialogues.text: Umm...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: It's alright, I'm not trying to make things difficult for you. I'll take note of the cancellation.

dialogues.speaker: Leeann
dialogues.text: Thank you... I'm really sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Don't worry about it. Just let me know if there's anything I can do to help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is it just Paimon, or was she acting a bit strange just now... Wonder why she wouldn't tell us why she was cancelling her order...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: It's not a big deal. These things happen every once in a while.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: A family emergency, an important payday falling through, a lovers' quarrel, no one to take you to the ball... I've pretty much heard it all.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Judging from the look on her face, something's keeping her from revealing the truth to us. It's best not to pry.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, guess this means you'll have more time to work on Fashion Week, right?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: That's true. Come, let's pick up where we left off...

dialogues.speaker: Weis
dialogues.text: ...Is Miss Chiori in?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: I am. How can I help you?

dialogues.speaker: Weis
dialogues.text: Um... I'd like to return this item.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Oh? Could I ask why?

dialogues.speaker: Weis
dialogues.text: It's just, um... not to my liking. You said I could get a refund if I wasn't satisfied, so... that's why I'm here.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Is there something about it that didn't meet your expectations? Are the sleeves too short, or is the color too dark? I can always make those adjustments for you.

dialogues.speaker: Weis
dialogues.text: Uh, no need... You don't have to concern yourself with that. I'd just like that refund please.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: And I'd be happy to process that for you... If you could just tell me the cause of your dissatisfaction...

dialogues.speaker: Guest Outside the Shop
dialogues.text: Is Chiori here? I'd like to return my outfit!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Another one!?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Is there some sort of new calamity coming that I haven't heard about? Another flood? Or an apocalypse maybe? What does the prophecy say this time — you'll be spared if you get rid of all your clothes?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Surely, the entire population of Fontaine didn't convene and pick this one day to come and return my clothes. What is going on?

dialogues.speaker: Guest Outside the Shop
dialogues.text: What kind of rags are you trying to sell us, huh? The way I see it, this shop is nothing more than a black market front run by a bunch of dirty criminals!

dialogues.speaker: Eloffe
dialogues.text: Please calm down, sir...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is he talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Weis
dialogues.text: Haven't you heard? Chioriya Boutique has been exposed for having close ties with criminals. It's all over the papers!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: And just who is it that dares to throw that accusation around?

dialogues.speaker: Weis
dialogues.text: Well, you tell us! The fabrics you've got here — they're all sourced from underground factories, aren't they?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: ...I've been transparent about my materials from the very beginning. I've already proved there's nothing wrong with them.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: If a little hearsay and baseless slander are enough to convince you, then by all means, go ahead and hand over your garments right now — spare yourself from that flood of yours. Or have you not been convinced of that one just yet...

dialogues.speaker: Weis
dialogues.text: You...!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Eloffe!

dialogues.speaker: Eloffe
dialogues.text: Miss Chiori...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Go outside and help these customers with their return requests. There's no need to ask them why. We'll refund them at the purchase price.

dialogues.speaker: Eloffe
dialogues.text: A—Alright...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: And once you're done, put up the sign that says we're closed for the day.

dialogues.speaker: Eloffe
dialogues.text: ...Got it.

dialogues.speaker: Weis
dialogues.text: Hmph...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chiori...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: These rumors...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: They couldn't be more fabricated if you tried. No need to worry about them. I'm sure they'll go away on their own in a few days.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: The real goal here is to divert my attention away from Fashion Week. The best response right now is to tune it out and focus on finalizing my designs.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If you say so... but Paimon still can't help but worry...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: The best way to respond to public skepticism is to let your work speak for itself. There will be no doubt about the quality of my work once my new designs are released — the public just has to see it for themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Eloffe
dialogues.text: ...Miss Chiori! Bad news!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Oh, for the love of... Can a woman not get a moment of peace to do her work? Go on. What's the matter now?

dialogues.speaker: Eloffe
dialogues.text: It's our accessories supplier. They just sent word that they'll no longer be able to supply us during Fashion Week!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: What? No accessories? Not even the ones we pre-ordered?

dialogues.speaker: Eloffe
dialogues.text: Yes, that's what their messenger said...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: And what about the models we asked them to book for us?

dialogues.speaker: Eloffe
dialogues.text: I think... They'll probably pull out as well...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Even the suppliers believe those nasty rumors!?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Is the messenger still here?

dialogues.speaker: Eloffe
dialogues.text: No, they've already left.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So no accessories means... no brooches, no bow ties, things like that?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Not just that. It means no gems, ribbons, gold thread — all the elements that lend life and soul to my designs.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... if you take those away... Does that mean you won't be able to make your designs at all?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: ...Eloffe, you stay and watch the shop. I'll go talk to the supplier myself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! And we can vouch for you too! We'll make sure your supplier knows there's nothing wrong with your clothes!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Thank you. In that case, please come with me.

choices.text: Maybe we'll be able to find out what happened.

dialogues.speaker: Wenger
dialogues.text: Who is it?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Wenger. It's Chiori.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: We've worked together all these years — the least you could do is allow me a face-to-face conversation.

dialogues.speaker: Wenger
dialogues.text: Haha... Straightforward as always, I see. You know, there are certain conventions people usually follow if they want to seek someone's company — sending a messenger for example.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: And when has following convention ever gotten me anywhere? Why hire a messenger when I can just explain things in person?

dialogues.speaker: Wenger
dialogues.text: Hmm... Have you read the papers today?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: I don't like to waste my time on baseless lies and speculation. Maybe that's something you should consider as well...

dialogues.speaker: Wenger
dialogues.text: You're right. I only subscribe to The Steambird, and most days, I never even read the others.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: So these rumors... The Steambird was the one that published them?

dialogues.speaker: Wenger
dialogues.text: No, not at all. They were in some second-rate fashion tabloids.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Well then, there you go! Those sort of headlines become old news faster than you can read them. Surely a bit of tabloid drama isn't worth cutting off my supply?

dialogues.speaker: Wenger
dialogues.text: *sigh* You would think that... But this time is different...

dialogues.speaker: Wenger
dialogues.text: Someone paid off the tabloids to publish the same article at once. They even went so far as to leave a copy in front of every house. That's how I first learned of the rumors.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Every house? That means... someone must have been planning this for a very long time...

dialogues.speaker: Wenger
dialogues.text: It seems your rival has really pulled out all the stops this time, Chiori. The article was even published alongside a photo of you...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: What sort of photo?

dialogues.speaker: Wenger
dialogues.text: A photo of you... beating up someone on the street yesterday.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yesterday!? Wait. That means...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Tsk... Uther again...

dialogues.speaker: Wenger
dialogues.text: Here, I've got a copy. See for yourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Behind the scenes, the true Chioriya Boutique takes shape — not a fashion house, but a house of lies...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Relying on its close ties to the criminal underworld, the Chioriya brand employs illegal competitive tactics to come out on top, giving hope to the evil-doers among us that wrongdoing can still prevail, provided you conceal it under the guise of fashion and beauty.

dialogues.speaker: Wenger
dialogues.text: I don't know what happened, and I don't want to comment on things that I didn't see with my own eyes. Still, that photo shows you to be the clear aggressor.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! He was the one who started it, that little...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I appreciate you standing up for me, Paimon, but it can't be helped now...

response.speaker: Wenger
response.text: That's right. The court of public opinion has already made up its mind... Still, I've got to give your rival high marks for effort. They even dug up the fact that my father once served time in the Fortress of Meropide...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: But that was so long ago...

response.speaker: Wenger
response.text: In the world of fashion, your past is like a piece of clothing stained with mud — once tainted, it can never be washed clean.

response.speaker: Wenger
response.text: They claim that most of your clientele are criminals and that those who buy your clothes are just like you — people who silence all dissent with violence.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: The absurdity... I don't even know which part to laugh at the most.

response.speaker: Wenger
response.text: Well, it's no laughing matter.

response.speaker: Wenger
response.text: Maybe your clientele are criminals, maybe they're not. There's even the possibility that they're just people who happened to commit crimes after buying your clothes...

response.speaker: Wenger
response.text: But, with the way this article combines fact with rumor, trying to determine the truth is practically an exercise in futility. It's not something people are just going to forget about in a day or two, especially when they've found several people to back up their claims.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: ...Wenger, are you sure you won't reconsider? If we go through with the show together, we can defeat them fair and square.

response.speaker: Wenger
response.text: Hahaha... If I were younger, I might have said yes.

response.speaker: Wenger
response.text: But I'm no longer that brave young man with nothing to lose. I've got the family business to consider now.

response.speaker: Wenger
response.text: I'd be perfectly happy to work with you again after this, but my daughter is manning the store during Fashion Week, and I don't want her implicated in all this. She doesn't deserve to be swarmed by all that negative publicity.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: ...I understand.

response.speaker: Wenger
response.text: Let me offer you a piece of advice, Chiori, for old time's sake — let this Fashion Week go. There's always next year. You just need to wait for all of this to blow over.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: You're free to wait things out, Wenger. I'll make my own choices.

response.speaker: Wenger
response.text: Heh... have you ever thought maybe that attitude of yours is what's gotten you into all this trouble?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Have you ever thought maybe this attitude of mine is precisely what paved the way for my success?

response.speaker: Wenger
response.text: Fair enough... Then I suppose all there's left to say is... Best of luck. As for the models... *sigh* None of them wanted to be implicated in all this either...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Understood. Take care.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, um... What should we do now?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Without the accessories, I can no longer use my old designs.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, how could they do this! They're making things up! The Boutique doesn't have anything to do with violent criminals! Can't people tell this is just a bunch of lies!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Public opinion has never been about what's true and what's not. It's about echoing the loudest voice in the room.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Tch... I should have seen it from the beginning. Uther knows me too well. Everything that happened yesterday... was just a trap.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, guess all we can do is just head back for now...

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Charlotte!? What are you doing here?

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Looking for you, of course! Did you see those fashion tabloids this morning?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean that sorry excuse for an article? Ugh, just thinking about it makes Paimon's blood boil!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: You too, huh?

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Whoever wrote that article must have known The Steambird would never print something so defamatory. Unfortunately, not all the papers in Fontaine share our same sense of journalistic integrity...

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Miss Chiori doesn't deserve to suffer all this baseless slander! I was just about to find some people to interview so that I can write an article to refute all those claims! If there's one thing I can't stand... it's people who misrepresent and distort the facts!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's great! With your help, we might be able to get some people back on our side!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: It's my pleasure! I've met Miss Chiori several times. I know she's not the kind of person that article makes her out to be.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: She was the one who made the hat and tie for my Kamera, "Monsieur Verite."

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Speaking of Miss Chiori, do you know where she went? Eloffe told me you all were together.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Huh? She was just here... Maybe she went over there. Let's go and check.

choices.text: He even hired some goons to attack her courier...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no... We've lost her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did you hear what all of those people were saying? Paimon can't believe they bought all that nonsense...

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Miss Chiori doesn't often appear in public or give a lot of interviews, so the general public hasn't had a chance to really get to know her.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: It's also true that her way of dealing with things can be a little... extreme sometimes. It's easy to use that to mislead people who don't know anything else about her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, this is all Uther's fault! Paimon would pick him up and throw him across the room too, if she could!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a second... You don't think Chiori might have gone looking for him, do you? Y'know, so she can, uh... finish what she started?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: That would only make the situation worse for her. I'm sure Miss Chiori knows that too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You've got a point... Let's just return to the boutique and see if she's there, then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eloffe! We're back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? Who's this?

dialogues.speaker: Eloffe
dialogues.text: Ah, this is Miss Laetitia. She's also here to see Miss Chiori.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! You're the one who came to collect the wedding dress yesterday, right? Wait, please don't say you're returning that dress, too...

dialogues.speaker: Laetitia
dialogues.text: Oh, no, no, not at all! I'm just here to thank her! In fact, if there's anything I can do to help her out, I'd be more than willing...

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Ah, so you've come across that article as well.

dialogues.speaker: Laetitia
dialogues.text: Yeah... You probably don't know this... But after I got engaged, I didn't think I'd be able to wear a Chioriya dress on my wedding day.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Why?

dialogues.speaker: Laetitia
dialogues.text: My fiance owns a small business. It doesn't bring in a lot of Mora, but we get by. After he proposed, he took me to Chioriya Boutique, and we put down a custom order for a dress.

dialogues.speaker: Laetitia
dialogues.text: He probably noticed how often I talked about Miss Chiori's clothes and how pretty they were... Being able to wear one of her dresses to my wedding has always been my dream.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: And then?

dialogues.speaker: Laetitia
dialogues.text: And then... Something happened to the business, and we ran into major Mora problems. We were able to scrounge up enough to pay off our debts, but... it left us without the funds to pay for the dress.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But didn't Chiori say she was able to make the dress from what was left of the original deposit?

dialogues.speaker: Laetitia
dialogues.text: Yes... When I came to cancel the order, she asked if something happened, and I told her everything...

dialogues.speaker: Laetitia
dialogues.text: She heard me out, and then told me not to worry. She assured me that the deposit I paid would be enough for the dress, and that she'd be able to finish making it in time as well... She promised that I'd be able to wear a Chioriya dress on my wedding day.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Well, that's a good thing isn't it? I've always known Miss Chiori to be a woman of her word.

dialogues.speaker: Laetitia
dialogues.text: It is good... It's just... After I went home yesterday, I couldn't help but take out the dress and try it on. My fiance happened to walk into the room... and when he saw me, he froze on the spot.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Ah... What a shame... He's not supposed to see it until the wedding day...

dialogues.speaker: Laetitia
dialogues.text: Well, see, that wasn't actually the issue...

dialogues.speaker: Laetitia
dialogues.text: He's seen a lot of wedding dresses in his time doing business, so as soon as he saw it, he knew for sure that it must've cost far more than what we paid.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Huh? So wait, that means...

dialogues.speaker: Laetitia
dialogues.text: Yeah... Miss Chiori covered all the costs and held nothing back. The fabric, accessories, beading, construction... It was all of the highest quality.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Miss Laetitia... I'd really like to use your story for a piece I'm writing about the boutique. Would you mind going on the record?

dialogues.speaker: Laetitia
dialogues.text: Huh? Well, if it would help Miss Chiori out, I wouldn't mind at all...

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: I think it'd go a long way! Your real experience is more powerful than all of those lies combined!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Eloffe... Has Chiori come back here since we left?

dialogues.speaker: Eloffe
dialogues.text: Huh? I thought you all were together...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we were... Hmm, if she didn't come back here, then do you know of any other places she could've gone?

dialogues.speaker: Eloffe
dialogues.text: Umm...

dialogues.speaker: Eloffe
dialogues.text: Oh, I remember now! There's this one cliff by the sea! Miss Chiori would always go there whenever she was upset.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: In that case, why don't we split up? I'll continue interviewing Miss Laetitia, and you two can go look for Miss Chiori.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, sounds good! Let's go!

talks.objective: Look for Chiori at the designated location

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There you are, Chiori!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Huh? How did you know where I... Ah, Eloffe told you, didn't she?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She did... We were just looking for you at your shop, and Laetitia was there! She wanted to thank you for the dress... So you see? You don't have to be sad! We'll figure out how to get through this together!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Ah, I'm not upset. I just wanted to get some fresh air.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Want to sit here with me? The view's quite stunning.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Don't worry, I'll catch you if you fall.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright. Don't mind if we do!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Well, how does it feel?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This place is pretty great!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Right? It's quiet and open, and far from the relentless critique from fashion commentators and the media. It's just you and the beautiful scenery.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! It's important to take yourself out of that kind of stressful environment every once in a while.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I didn't grow up in a very strict family. My parents would joke that I grew up to be so assertive because they spoiled me as a child.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I would get together with the other children to climb trees and explore caves... One time, I even climbed over the walls of the Kamisato Estate. One of the servants had to physically remove me...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa... Paimon would have never imagined that...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: But even as rambunctious as I was, when it came to needlework, I was as quiet and focused as could be.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: It was as if I'd discovered a whole new world within those vibrant, dazzling fabrics... You know the feeling?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Err, sorta...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: My parents noticed, and they sent me to study under a famous Inazuman tailor. It wasn't long before I had driven away pretty much every master tailor on the archipelago. You could say I really tried their patience.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You were that misbehaved?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I wasn't misbehaved, exactly. I just... often had strange ideas when it came to fashion, ones that weren't in line with traditional ways of doing things.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: On top of that, I hated the idea of groveling and making outfits for every arrogant big shot expecting me to be at their beck and call.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Anyway, a few incidents later, I soon found myself without a master. Worse, not one shop was willing to hire me, not even to do grunt work.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No wonder you left Inazuma...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I was angry and frustrated, so before I left, I swore to all those "masters" that my brand would one day become renowned all over Teyvat.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, that's a great dream to strive towards!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: After that, I came all the way to the Court of Fontaine — a city often referred to as the capital of arts and fashion.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I had a lot of fun starting out. Sure, I was living in a small, cramped room... but I was finally free to make whatever I wanted.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I had a far more naive view of "fashion" back then. As long as something was pretty, it would become popular, right? A simple concept, surely.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Of course, as I spent more and more time in the industry, I learned nothing was ever that simple, least of all "fashion."

choices.text: Well, I know someone who absolutely adored your designs...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Oh, you mean Laetitia?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Yeah, she did mention that dream... I'll be honest with you. That's the first time I ever heard something like that from one of my customers.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Who would have thought... Even as I continue to pursue my dream, my work has also become someone else's...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Alright, that's enough sight-seeing for one day. Time to come up with a way out of this mess.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh! Looks like you've got your game face back!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Back? It was never gone to begin with. I did say I wasn't upset, didn't I?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks we should look for evidence that Uther wrote that article, and that he hired those Treasure Hoarders to attack Kirara!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Charlotte's already working on an article to address all those nasty rumors, so we can publish all our findings in The Steambird once we're done!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I don't like duking it out in the press... But if Charlotte's thrown her hat in the ring, I won't stop her, either.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I know where Uther's clothing factory is located. It might be a good place to start looking for some evidence.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds good! We'll come with!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: As for Fashion Week... Well, there's always next year, right? So there's no need to be too upset!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Hmm? When did this become an either-or situation? Find incriminating evidence, or participate in Fashion Week? Hah, I'm doing both.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? But your accessories... Didn't you say your designs were unusable without them?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Well, it's true that I haven't quite figured out what to do about that, but...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: To tell you the truth... Even here in Fontaine, every time I see the sea, I can't help but remember Inazuma... and the vow I made in front of those "masters"...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Thinking about all that, I just... can't bear to take even one step back.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: ...The sea...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm? What did you just say, Chiori?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: ...The sea. Seashells... Coral...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: ...I've got it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Got what?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Come! Let's take a dip, shall we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!? Chiori, wait, hold up!

choices.text: And dreamed of wearing one at her wedding...
It doesn't look like there's a lot of space...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Ah, sorry about that. I'm the only one here most of the time.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Please organize the clothes with an eye towards their types and styles. I'm counting on you.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Hmm, not bad. You might just have an eye for design.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: ...You didn't get bought out by my competitors, did you? This arrangement... It's...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: ...Never mind. It might look like a chaotic mess, but I suppose it works as a change of pace — and who knows? This style arrangement might come into vogue someday.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These should be enough, right? Paimon picked all the prettiest ones in this area!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chiori! Will these do?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Hmm... everything looks great. I've also collected a pretty big batch, so we should have enough.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great! So, are we gonna head back now and make some new designs?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Yes, but don't forget, we've got more than just the designs to worry about when we get back.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Okay, we've got the materials for the accessories. Next... we'll need to use what we have on hand to create some new outfits.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean we have to start from scratch? Will there be enough time?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: I should be able to make it... if I skip out on sleep.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nuh-uh, skipping out on sleep is not the answer! Wait... How come this conversation is giving Paimon major deja vu...

choices.text: Sounds pretty similar to one we've had with Ganyu before.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Ganyu? Who's that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A friend of ours who does way too much overtime!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, anyway... Sleep is important! You're not gonna convince Paimon otherwise!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Haha, well I can't argue with you there. One thing's for sure, though — I'm going to do whatever it takes to make it work.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Hah... All this grit and determination... It reminds me of the first Fashion Week I ever participated in...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What else can we help with?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Hmm... Let me see...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I suppose all there's left to do is... tear up all the outfits currently on display.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You got it! Uh... Wait, what did you just say!?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: You heard me. Tear them all up.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: When I went to that first Fashion Week, I had no savings to speak of, just a few dozen yards of fabric and a dream.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I had to make something work, so I tore up all the clothes that I brought with me from Inazuma, and I used the scraps to make my entries for the show. I used the larger pieces for the base fabric and the smaller pieces for accessories...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: If it worked back then, why not now? We can also repurpose some of the ready-to-use accessories in the shop as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... You worked so hard on all these outfits...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I know. That's why I refuse to let it all go to waste. I'm not going to let them win, even if it takes everything I've ever made and more.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, okay... Then, here goes nothing...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: No need to be nervous. I won't hold it against you.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Of course, if anyone dared to tear up one of my dresses in front of me on a normal day, I'd probably toss them into the sewer.

choices.text: I guess going after what you want means making certain sacrifices.

dialogues.speaker: Eloffe
dialogues.text: I know Miss Chiori has put a lot of work into making Fashion Week a success...

dialogues.speaker: Eloffe
dialogues.text: I hope you can talk things through with the supplier.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lyney, Lynette! Great, you're both here!

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: A moment later and you'd have missed us.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: We read the article in the papers — we were just about to go find Miss Chiori.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: She helped design a number of our costumes in the past and even sponsored one of our performances. The time has come, it seems, for us to return the favor.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, perfect! She was the one who sent us!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: In that case, I assume that there's something we can do to help? Just say the word, and we'll take care of it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, so it's like this...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: ...Is that all we'll need to do?

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Should be a piece of cake for the two of us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, Paimon's glad to hear it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well then... Guess it's about time we go and find some evidence for all the bad stuff Uther has been doing, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chiori said we shouldn't disturb her over the next couple of days. We can check in with her again once she's done with all the new designs.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: But the show's in another two days, isn't it? Will she be able to make the deadline?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, according to her, she wants to first beat Uther fair and square at the show, and then defeat him in the court of public opinion. She said that it'd be like, uh...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: A two-pronged approach?

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Courtesy first, confrontation second?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... Yeah, something like that.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Understood. Then we'll have faith in her decision. We'll go make some preparations — see you at the venue in two days.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright! We're counting on you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, then let's also do as Chiori said and meet up with her at Uther's factory in two days. We'll gather the evidence then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon sure hopes she won't have a hard time making all of those new outfits for the show...

dialogues.speaker: Graciette
dialogues.text: Fashion Week is coming up! My husband promised to get me a replica of the most eye-catching outfit from the show.

dialogues.speaker: Trudaine
dialogues.text: Oh, I say! As expected of a high-flying merchant! How generous of him!

dialogues.speaker: Trudaine
dialogues.text: Well, what a coincidence, though — my husband promised me precisely the same thing!

dialogues.speaker: Graciette
dialogues.text: Oh dear! Whatever are we going to do, then, if we fall in love with the same dress?

dialogues.speaker: Trudaine
dialogues.text: Well, let's leave our gentlemen to figure that one out for themselves, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Fashion Week Promotional Poster
dialogues.text: The much-anticipated Fontaine Fashion Week has begun!

dialogues.speaker: Fashion Week Promotional Poster
dialogues.text: Many renowned designers have gathered for this event. Their meticulously crafted, brand-new works will be on display during the final show.

dialogues.speaker: Fashion Week Promotional Poster
dialogues.text: Let the light of fashion shine upon the City of the Arts!

dialogues.speaker: Graciette
dialogues.text: ...It's Fashion Week right now...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Speaking of clothes... Do yours happen to need any mending right now, Kirara?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Ehehehe... Well since you asked, Chiori, there's this part around my waist...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Oh? Need a bit of letting out around the middle?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: No! It's a tear! Those bad guys did it!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: So, in your opinion, what is Miss Chiori like as a person?

dialogues.speaker: Laetitia
dialogues.text: Let's see... Well, she's certainly not afraid to say what she means, but she always looks out for her customers however she can...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: What should we do about these clothes everywhere? Need any help?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Sort them by the type of fabric first, and then by color. Oh and, don't forget to remove any accessories and put them to the side.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: That sounds pretty straightforward. I'll help, too!

dialogues.speaker: Graciette
dialogues.text: Did you read the paper today?

dialogues.speaker: Trudaine
dialogues.text: Oh I did! My goodness, I couldn't believe what I was reading!

dialogues.speaker: Graciette
dialogues.text: Do you think there's any truth to it? Have you asked your husband? He's a judge isn't he?

dialogues.speaker: Trudaine
dialogues.text: Pfft, he would never indulge in such idle gossip! Still, he advised me to hold off on buying any more related wares for the time being.

dialogues.speaker: Graciette
dialogues.text: Yes, how prudent — wait for the dust to settle. My husband said the same.

dialogues.speaker: Trudaine
dialogues.text: Indeed, indeed! I wouldn't want to invite scandal through one of my purchases, now would I?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: By the way, we really are just going to "talk," right?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Of course. I wouldn't do anything to one of my business partners, especially when a reasonable conversation should suffice.

dialogues.speaker: Person Idly Chatting by the Roadside
dialogues.text: If you ask me, I think Chioriya Boutique is done for.

dialogues.speaker: Person Idly Chatting by the Roadside
dialogues.text: I mean, what did they expect? Engaging with criminals behind their customers' backs...

dialogues.speaker: Person Idly Chatting by the Roadside
dialogues.text: They kept up a solid front, though. I've even bought from them before...

dialogues.speaker: Person Idly Chatting by the Roadside
dialogues.text: Really? How was it?

dialogues.speaker: Person Idly Chatting by the Roadside
dialogues.text: The owner was plenty fierce, that's for sure. Makes sense if she regularly deals with criminals, I guess. I've got the chills just thinking about it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chioriii! Why did you just jump into the sea all of a sudden?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Paimon, what do you think is the most beautiful thing in the sea?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Erm... A Lumitoile? Or a pearl maybe... Ooh, coral's pretty too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! Paimon gets it now... You want to use things like that as the "accessories" for your designs!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Well, now that you've hit the nail on the head, help me grab some, would you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Leave it to us!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Just this once, though, I think I can make an exception. Go ahead and tear them up. Think of it as a good way to vent your emotions.

dialogues.speaker: Graciette
dialogues.text: Did you read the paper today?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You return to the boutique with Chiori...
